questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The wide range of possibilities to experience classical music, opera and culture in general.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the information I needed to know upon arrival was very easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where two intro meetings with general information, but everything I needed to know was provided in E-mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They provided a lot of information and multiple times.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. There where a lot of cheap dormitory oportunities in central Vienna and close to the various university buildings.
Know that there where also a lot of others that found private accomodation very easily on facebook and so on.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The dormitory is cheap, but also a bit ugly and not too charming. But the location was great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Uni Wien have a very bad system, both for exchange students but also just in general. 
You need to have a lot of patience as waiting lists and late admission is the standard way to do it in there system. But everything somehow works out for all, so you have to keep calm and trust that you will get into the courses you need.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Look at the additional comment above. Everybody register for a lot of courses since there are only limited amount that are admitted. So everybody rush in the registration face, but also a lot de-register in the beginning of the semester, and if you are in top 10 on the waiting list you will likely be admitted to the course, althogh it may be a week or two into the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote some panicking emails, but they just told me to have patience. And it turned out it was true.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got the 30 ECTS I wanted, but since there where not a lot of courses that I could take, I just feel I took the courses I could

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm, it is chaotic and very bad, but trust that it somehow works out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In general the academic level is very low, and exams hard since they are very old-school short time no tools allowed. Hence exam most of all test your ability to recognize patterns and remember, not your ability to think.
The short semester forces students to just focus on exam, not in actual learning making it a very demotivating study environment. No academic curiosity, no motivation. Just the necessity to pass exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very low level in general. Most MA courses I took was 1-year BA level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More conservative and old school. Only 90 min lectures with no break. 
Of course there existed exemption for one or two courses, where it was a small class and open discussion, but in general very borring lectures with old professors with no patience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Economtrics in Finance (8 ECTS, the only challenging course, with a professor that actual expected something)
- Modelling bounded Rationality (8 ECTS,small class open discussion, quite funny but not super usesull)
- Basics of Finance (4 ECTS, very old school, and hard exam, short time and learning by heart instead of learn to think and reason)
- Economic Psycology (4 ECTS, disturbing low level)
- Topics in Economic Policy (4 ECTS, disturbing low level)
- Vienna International Economics Seminar (2 ECTS, interesting presentations of newest reaseach)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Look at description above, I actually learned something usefull in Econometrics in Finance as the only course I would say.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very sad faculty.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware of any, but I think there are sport opportunities if you look for it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you as me like classical concerts, operas and theatre, Vienna is unique. And have great discuount for young people. Best seats in the opera and Musikverein for only 20 EUR.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Walk around and take your time taking in the beautiful city. Walk into a cafe and experience the nice cafe culture they have.'+´´´´´´

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Culture kind of similar to danish, but of course minor details you learn along the way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak with them in the firsts lecutes. Most of them I talked to was very open to talk and curious to get to know new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Conservative classical culture. Of course also a lot of touristy places, but if you look careful you will find local gems.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Do not expect high academic level or a motivating study environment.
- Semester is short, so enjoy a free first month (september/february) before semester begins and be prepared for a stressful last month where lectures and exams overlaps.
- Enjoy the atmosphere and imperical vibes in the city. Fills you with energy and motivation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is of course the entire Erasmus community where it is all about partying and experience top 10 tourist activities.
If you are not into these superficial communities the intragram page Befriend_Vienna is a nice alternative to get to know new people. Both local and other foreigners.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the classical culture I got to experience. Will never see so many plays, operas and concerts in such a short amount of time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That not many people seems to care about the unigue cultural atmosphere in Vienna and just wanted to locate the cheapest beers.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
